propositions: R1/R2 mechanism rules (no raw subprocess git) are insufficient; the protocol rule (mutations via atomic transaction) requires a new composition rule R3 that fires when mutation primitives are called outside the seam-internal modules.

R3 must bind on the receiver (resolved git-adapter module reference via import or dynamic-loader binding) rather than bare attribute names to avoid false positives on ubiquitous methods like set.add() and session.commit().

Two out-of-transaction sites require durable reasoned inline markers: reconcile_helpers.py's selective 5-file staging and __main__.py's detached-index CAS purge; both are architecturally sound but cannot route through the offered commit seams without changing behavior.
The receiver-binding resolver must resolve two binding forms per file: import bindings (including as-aliases) and dynamic-loader bindings via module-path string argument.
R3's sanctioned entry set (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py) must be keyed on exact repo-relative path, not just filename, to prevent bypass via lookalike filenames in other packages.
False-positive floor (set.add, session.commit, git_adapter read exports like commit_email) must remain silent; unit tests confirm zero violations on non-git-adapter callables and readonly operations.
